row.question:
Based on the chest X-ray findings in Figure 2, which of the following is the most likely diagnosis given the patient’s clinical presentation and history of COPD with bullous emphysema?
A) Tension pneumothorax
B) Giant bulla
C) Tension bulla
D) Atypical pneumothorax
E) Pleural effusion
F) Consolidation

reflection_candidates.json.condition: When CXR shows a new unilateral upper/mid-lung opacity in a patient with electrical injury and no trauma/surgery, and the opacity abuts the hilum without diaphragmatic silhouetting
reflection_candidates.json.action: Inspect for loss of hilar silhouette (silhouette sign) and absence of meniscus or visceral pleural line; assess for air bronchograms to favor consolidation over atelectasis or effusion
reflection_candidates.json.limitation: Fails if overpenetration obscures subtle opacities or if lateral view unavailable; cannot distinguish infection from thermal injury without clinical context

reflection_candidates.json.condition: When a new unilateral hemithorax opacity appears after resolution of prior ipsilateral opacity, and mediastinal shift is toward the new opacity
reflection_candidates.json.action: Inspect for loss of lung volume (flattened diaphragm, crowding of ribs, tracheal deviation) and absence of meniscus sign to favor atelectasis over effusion
reflection_candidates.json.limitation: Fails if poor inspiration or overpenetration masks volume loss; does not differentiate mucus plugging from tumor/foreign body without clinical data
